newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Suharto calls for ASEAN business cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Suharto calls for ASEAN business cooperation.

text.p: Indonesia's President Suharto opened a two-day ASEAN business meeting on Wednesday with a call for private enterprise to cooperate to meet the challenges of open markets and free trade.
"Open economy and free trade will not only strengthen the cooperation among nations but also tighten the competition.

"If Southeast Asian nations are unable to remain united, we will lose the available opportunities. Hopefully, for this reason, this meeting will promote further the business communities in ASEAN," he said.

The first business summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) has brought together business leaders from the region and its major trading partners from Asia, Europe and North America.

The ASEAN Free Trade Area (AFTA) plans to cut tariffs within the region on some 40,000 lines of products to zero-to-five percent by the year 2003. Some sensitive agricultural products, such as rice and sugar, will continue to receive protection for some years under a temporary exclusion list.
Suharto told the gathering that ASEAN's geographic location and abundant economic resources made it a strategic production base.
"The increasingly rapid (economic) liberalisation process will simultaneously offer new market opportunities and new challenges," he said.
"I hope ASEAN businessmen can develop new initiatives for the promotion of small and medium enterprises which have great potential for the creation of employment opportunities....," he said.

Suharto also called for a reliable partnership between business and government and "a common ASEAN vision" to lead the region towards its goals of economic liberalisation and free trade over the next couple of decades.
ASEAN currently comprises Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, the Philippines, Vietnam and Brunei.
Cambodia, Laos and Burma are expected to join the bloc later this year.
